title: Resonant Coherent Breathing
description: Breathe at a rate of 5.5 to 6 breaths per minute to maximize heart rate variability and optimize autonomic nervous system balance.
steps: Sit in an upright, relaxed posture with your spine straight and feet flat on the floor.
Inhale gently through your nose for 5.0 seconds, letting your abdomen expand naturally.
Without pausing, exhale slowly and smoothly through your mouth or nose for 5.0 seconds.
Maintain this continuous, rhythmic cycle for the duration of the practice.
Focus your attention on the smooth transitions between the inhalation and exhalation.
scienceDescription: Engages respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA) and baroreflex loops to maximize HRV amplitude. Promotes high parasympathetic vagal tone and restores prefrontal connectivity.

title: The Physiological Sigh
description: A rapid autonomic reset to discharge accumulated carbon dioxide, slow heart rate, and deactivate acute sympathetic stress responses.
steps: Inhale deeply through your nose, expanding your chest.
At the very peak of the inhalation, take a sharp, quick secondary sip of air to fully expand your lungs' alveoli.
Exhale fully through your mouth with a slow, relaxed, long sighing sound ('ahhh').
Repeat this cycle of double-inhale followed by an extended sigh 3 to 5 times.
Pause and observe the immediate reduction in physical muscle tension.
scienceDescription: Double inhalation opens collapsed alveoli, increasing surface area for rapid CO2 removal. The subsequent extended exhale activates the vagal brake, triggering immediate parasympathetic dominance.

title: Tactical Box Breathing
description: An equal-ratio breathing technique used by elite practitioners to stabilize arousal, reduce hypervigilance, and restore cognitive clarity.
steps: Exhale all air from your lungs.
Inhale slowly through your nose for a count of 4.
Hold your breath at the top for a count of 4, keeping your airway and throat relaxed.
Exhale smoothly through your mouth for a count of 4.
Hold your lungs empty at the bottom for a count of 4.
Repeat the complete cycle for 4-5 rounds or until your system feels grounded.
scienceDescription: The balanced ratios of inhale, hold, exhale, hold act as an autonomic modulator, preventing runaway sympathetic hyperarousal while maintaining active, focused arousal.

title: Trauma-Informed 5-4-3-2-1 Sensory Grounding
description: Reorient your system to the safety of the current environment and present moment when experiencing hyperarousal, flashbacks, or panic.
steps: Pause and take one slow, grounding breath.
Look around you and name 5 distinct things you can see (e.g., a pen, a spot on the wall, a tree outside).
Notice your physical body and touch 4 things you can feel (e.g., the texture of your pants, the cold table, the chair under you).
Listen closely and identify 3 sounds you can hear (e.g., a distant car, hum of a fan, birds chirping).
Focus on your senses and identify 2 things you can smell or recall smelling.
Bring awareness to your mouth and name 1 thing you can taste, or notice the current neutral state of your palate.
scienceDescription: Recruits cortical processing and sensory thalamic pathways to redirect neural resources away from the hyperactive amygdala. Signals environmental safety to the brainstem to break hypervigilant threat loops.

title: Somatic Orienting & Freeze Mobilization
description: Gently cue safety to your brainstem to lift your system out of a shut-down, flatlined, or dissociated Dorsal Vagal state without triggering anxiety.
steps: Slowly let your eyes scan the room. Notice and name out loud 3 objects that are blue, then 3 objects that are green.
Gently rub your hands together, generating physical heat and friction. Press your warm palms to your cheeks.
Wrap your arms around your torso, squeezing firmly to feel your body's physical boundaries in space.
Slowly press your feet flat into the floor, feeling the physical support and resistance of the ground beneath you.
Gently roll your shoulders back and take a shallow, comfortable breath, letting out a soft hum on the exhale.
scienceDescription: Engages visual and somatosensory orienting networks to communicate current ambient safety. Activates gentle sympathetic mobilization to lift the system out of the metabolic conservation mode of Dorsal freeze.

title: Jacobson Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR)
description: A systematic somatic exercise of tensing and releasing key muscle groups to cultivate deep interoceptive awareness and somatic calm.
steps: Lie down flat or sit comfortably, closing your eyes if it feels safe to do so.
Focus on your feet. Inhale, curl your toes down, and squeeze them tightly for 5 seconds.
Exhale and release all tension instantly, letting your feet relax and feel heavy. Pause for 10 seconds.
Move up to your calves, thighs, glutes, abdomen, chest, shoulders, hands, and facial muscles.
At each muscle group, tense for 5 seconds, then release completely for 10 seconds, feeling the deep contrast of relaxation.
scienceDescription: Physically tensing muscles triggers a reflex relaxation response upon release. Exercises somatic interoceptive pathways, decreasing allostatic muscle shielding and lowering resting heart rate.

title: Circadian Sleep Consolidation
description: Align your bedtime routine to improve sleep efficiency and consolidate deep sleep architecture, crucial for traumatic memory integration.
steps: Maintain a strictly fixed wake time every morning, regardless of how much you slept the night before.
Calculate your actual sleep duration from your Apple Watch. Limit your time in bed to that duration plus 30 minutes.
Avoid blue light exposure from screens for at least 60 minutes before bedtime.
Keep the bedroom cool (optimal: 18°C / 65°F) to mimic and support the natural nocturnal core temperature drop.
If you are unable to fall asleep after 20 minutes in bed, get up, go to another dimly lit room, and do a calm somatic grounding exercise until tired.
scienceDescription: Restores circadian amplitude and maximizes homeostatic sleep drive. Consolidates sleep stages, ensuring optimal deep sleep (Slow Wave Sleep / N3) for glymphatic clearance and REM sleep for fear extinction.

title: Pre-Bed HRV Resonance Biofeedback
description: A deliberate pre-bed biofeedback breathing protocol to trigger a strong parasympathetic surge and reduce nocturnal hyperarousal.
steps: Sit on the edge of your bed in a comfortable, relaxed upright position.
Begin slow, paced breathing at 6 breaths per minute (5-second inhale, 5-second exhale).
Imagine the breath flowing directly into and out of your heart center, feeling the physical warmth of each breath.
Continue for 10 minutes, letting go of any cognitive planning or analytical thinking.
Lie down immediately after completion, carrying the physical sense of heavy, warm calm into your sleep.
scienceDescription: Maximizes respiratory sinus arrhythmia and overnight HRV recovery (SDNN delta), down-regulating sympathetic tone to reduce sleep onset latency and minimize nighttime awakenings.
